verses.text: “When that happens,” says the LORD, “they’ll pull the bones of Judah’s kings and princes, its priests and prophets, and the people of Jerusalem out of their graves.

They’ll scatter the bones in front of the sun, the moon, and all the host of heaven that those people loved and served, followed, sought out, and worshiped. Nobody will gather the bones or bury them. They’ll lie on the ground like manure.
Everyone left from this evil family, wherever they survive in the places I’ve driven them, will choose death over life,” says the LORD of Armies.
“Tell them this too: ‘The LORD says, “When people fall, don’t they get back up? When someone turns away, don’t they turn back?
Then why are the people of Jerusalem always turning farther away? They hang on to lies and refuse to come back.
I listened closely. What they said wasn’t right. Nobody turns from their evil and says, ‘What have I done?’ Everybody charges down their own path like a horse plunging straight into battle.
Even the stork up in the sky knows when it’s time to go. The turtledove, the swallow, and the crane all know when to come back. But my people don’t know the LORD’s law.
“‘How can you say, “We’re wise, and we have the LORD’s law”? Look, the scribes have used their lying pens to make that claim a lie.
Those wise men will be let down. They’ll be shaken and caught in a trap. They’ve rejected the LORD’s word. So what kind of wisdom do they have?

That’s why I’ll give their wives to other people and their fields to new owners. From the least to the greatest, everybody’s out to get more for themselves. From prophet to priest, nobody deals honestly.
They’ve barely touched my people’s wound and called it healed, saying, “Peace, peace,” when there’s no peace.

Did they feel ashamed when they did something disgusting? They had no shame at all. They couldn’t even blush. So they’ll go down with the others who fall. When I come to hold them to account, they’ll be brought down, says the LORD.
“‘I’ll wipe them out completely, says the LORD. There’ll be no grapes on the vine, no figs on the fig tree, and the leaves will wither. What I gave them will slip away from them.’”

“Why are we just sitting here? Get together! Let’s get inside the fortified cities and be silent there. The LORD our God has silenced us and given us poisoned water to drink, because we’ve sinned against the LORD.
We waited for peace, but nothing good came. We waited for a time to heal, and look what we got: terror!

You can hear his horses snorting all the way from Dan. The whole land shakes at the sound of his mighty horses neighing. They’ve come and swallowed up the land and everything in it, the city and everyone living there.”
“Look, I’ll send venomous snakes among you that nobody can charm. They’ll bite you,” says the LORD.
If only I could find some comfort in this grief! My heart is giving out inside me.
Listen to my people crying from a land far away: “Isn’t the LORD in Zion? Isn’t her King there?” “Why did they make me angry with their carved images and foreign idols?”
“The harvest is over. Summer’s gone, and we still haven’t been saved.”
My people are hurting, and it hurts me too. I’m grieving. I can’t shake the horror.
Is there no healing balm in Gilead? Is there no doctor there? Then why haven’t my people gotten well?
